    Pulling back unit forms; inflations #

    For a ℤ-linear map T with B(T e_a, T e_a) = 2, the form x ↦ q(T x) is again a unit form (UnitForm.pullback). An inflation (von Höhne 1988, 1.2) is the pullback along T_ab : x ↦ x - x_b e_a when q_ab = 1. Nonnegativity is preserved, and the radical vector y of q becomes y + y_b e_a.
